```jsx
<DateField.Root className={styles.Root}>
  {(section) => (
    <DateField.Section key={section.index} className={styles.Section} section={section} />
  )}

```

Why not e.g. `DateField.Month`, `DateField.Day`, `DateField.Year`, `DateField.Separator`?

## Codex Review

### Overview
This patch adds new `DateField`, `TimeField`, and `DateTimeField` primitives and pushes a lot of shared temporal logic into the existing calendar, localization, and validation layers. The feature work is substantial, but the branch also introduces a few regressions on existing public APIs and on the new fields’ form and accessibility behavior.

### Findings
#### 1. 🔴 [Blocking] Invalid temporal fields are not focusable on submit

**Impact**: When a form submission fails validation on one of the new temporal fields, focus does not move to that field. That breaks the form-level “focus the first invalid control” behavior and makes recovery slower for keyboard users.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/selectors.ts:192` wires `useField` with `controlRef: inputRef`, and `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/useTemporalFieldRoot.tsx:170` attaches that ref to the root `<div role="group">`. The field contract at `packages/react/src/field/useField.ts:89` expects a focusable control, and `packages/react/src/form/Form.tsx:41`, `packages/react/src/form/Form.tsx:68`, and `packages/react/src/form/Form.tsx:111` call `.focus()` on that ref when validation fails. This is inferred from the code path rather than reproduced in the browser, but the contract mismatch is direct.

**Recommendation**: Register a genuinely focusable element as `controlRef` for these fields, or make the root reliably focusable and redirect focus into the active section when the form targets it.

#### 2. 🔴 [Blocking] Calendar’s existing validation API is renamed incompatibly

**Impact**: Existing `Calendar` consumers using `minDate` / `maxDate`, or branching on the old `before-min-date` / `after-max-date` validation codes, will silently break in a PR that is otherwise presented as adding new field components.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/calendar/root/CalendarRoot.tsx:81` and `packages/react/src/calendar/root/CalendarRoot.tsx:128` now consume `min` / `max`, and the generated docs at `docs/reference/generated/calendar-root.json:58` only advertise those new prop names. At the same time, `packages/react/src/utils/temporal/validateDate.ts:15` now returns `rangeUnderflow` / `rangeOverflow`, which `packages/react/src/calendar/store/SharedCalendarStore.ts:195` surfaces through `getValidationError()`.

**Recommendation**: Keep the existing `Calendar` surface stable in this PR, or add a compatibility/deprecation layer for both the old prop names and the old validation result strings before merging.

#### 3. 🟡 [Non-blocking] Focus lands on sections that do not carry the field’s label or descriptions

**Impact**: A screen reader user interacting with the per-section `spinbutton`s can miss the field label and any linked error/help text, so multiple temporal fields become harder to distinguish and validation messaging is easier to miss.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/useTemporalFieldRoot.tsx:170` puts `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` on the non-focusable `role="group"` wrapper, while the focused sections are created from `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/selectors.ts:237` with only generic per-part labels like `Month`, `Day`, or `Hours`. This is inferred from the DOM/ARIA wiring rather than reproduced with assistive technology.

**Recommendation**: Ensure the focused section elements expose the field-level label and descriptions as well, rather than keeping that metadata only on the wrapper.

#### 4. 🟡 [Non-blocking] The clear button is removed from the Tab order by default

**Impact**: Keyboard users cannot reach the new public clear action with Tab unless they know to override the component props themselves.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/selectors.ts:285` hard-codes `tabIndex: -1` in the clear button props, and `packages/react/src/date-field/clear/DateFieldClear.tsx:37` forwards those props onto a real `<button>`. Because `TimeField.Clear` and `DateTimeField.Clear` reuse the same part, the issue applies to all three components.

**Recommendation**: Let the native button stay tabbable by default, or only opt it out of the Tab order when there is another documented keyboard path to reach the same action.

#### 5. 🟡 [Non-blocking] Reference data goes stale after `timezone` / `referenceDate` / bounds updates

**Impact**: If a consumer changes `timezone`, `referenceDate`, `min`, or `max` after mount, the next edit can still merge against the old reference date/time. That can produce surprising values until the actual field value changes.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:132` computes `referenceValue` once in the constructor and stores it in state at `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:176`. Later renders only sync the raw props via `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/useTemporalFieldRoot.tsx:133`, and the store’s derived observers at `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:215` rebuild format/sections but never recompute `referenceValue`. Edits still merge against `selectors.referenceValue(...)` at `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:527`.

**Recommendation**: Re-derive `referenceValue` whenever the props that feed it change, or derive it from the current synced props instead of treating it as constructor-only state.

#### 6. 🟡 [Non-blocking] Selection sync is tied to the global document instead of the field’s owner document

**Impact**: Focus and text-selection behavior can break when these fields are rendered in iframes or other non-main documents.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:987` correctly gets the selection from `ownerDocument(...)`, but `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:998` checks `instanceof Node` against the global constructor and `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:1007` creates the range with `new window.Range()`. In multi-document embeddings those globals can belong to the wrong browsing context.

**Recommendation**: Use the owning document and window consistently for both the `Node` check and range creation.

#### 7. ℹ️ [Informational] Section prop memoization effectively thrashes across siblings

**Impact**: Typing work scales more like “recompute every section” than “update only the edited section”, which is avoidable overhead in the hottest interaction path.

**Evidence**: Every section subscribes via `packages/react/src/date-field/section/DateFieldSection.tsx:39`, but the backing selector in `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/selectors.ts:215` uses `createSelectorMemoized`, whose implementation at `packages/utils/src/store/createSelector.ts:135` only stores one memoized selector instance per store state. Sibling section calls therefore evict each other’s selector arguments and force repeated `sectionProps` recomputation.

**Recommendation**: Move `sectionProps` to a per-section memoization strategy, or avoid a selector cache shape that only holds one argument tuple for all mounted sections.

#### 8. ℹ️ [Informational] Invalid-date editing relies on a fragile side channel and zero-delay timers

**Impact**: The current control flow is hard to reason about and easy to regress when the invalid-date path changes, because `value`, `sections`, and “what the user just typed” are not coming from a single source of truth.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:94` introduces `sectionToUpdateOnNextInvalidDate`, and the interaction between `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:456`, `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:520`, and `packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts:1213` uses that mutable field plus zero-delay timers to preserve typed text across invalid intermediate states.

**Recommendation**: Move the pending invalid-section state into store state or isolate this branch into a dedicated helper/state machine so the sequencing is explicit.

#### 9. ℹ️ [Informational] `TimeField` and `DateTimeField` duplicate the same hidden-input serialization pipeline

**Impact**: A future fix to rounding, `step`, or min/max serialization is easy to land in one field type and miss in the other.

**Evidence**: `packages/react/src/time-field/root/timeFieldConfig.ts:15` and `packages/react/src/date-time-field/root/dateTimeFieldConfig.ts:15` both implement the same pattern for native-value formatting, “always include seconds for min/max”, `step` scaling, and validation-attribute serialization with only minor differences in the format string.

**Recommendation**: Extract a shared helper for native temporal hidden-input config and let each field supply only the type-specific formatter and input type.

#### 10. ℹ️ [Informational] The riskiest interaction paths still have thin component-level coverage

**Impact**: Some of the branch’s most browser-sensitive behavior could regress without the current tests noticing.

**Evidence**: The shared form tests at `packages/react/test/temporalFieldRoot.shared-tests.tsx:212` and `packages/react/test/temporalFieldRoot.shared-tests.tsx:335` do not cover the partial-entry `'invalid'` sentinel / `badInput` path. The clear API coverage in `packages/react/src/date-field/root/DateFieldRoot.test.tsx:19` and `packages/react/src/date-field/root/DateFieldRoot.test.tsx:97` only exercises the happy path. The interaction suites at `packages/react/test/temporalFieldRoot.shared-interaction-tests.tsx:75`, `packages/react/src/time-field/root/TimeFieldRoot.interaction.test.tsx:24`, and `packages/react/src/date-time-field/root/DateTimeFieldRoot.interaction.test.tsx:24` still leave `paste`, `Delete`, and `Escape` largely untested at the component level. Locale-sensitive default-format rendering is also only lightly exercised compared with the amount of logic now depending on it.

**Recommendation**: Add component-level regressions for partial-entry form validation, imperative and guarded clear behavior, locale-driven default section order/separators, and the `paste` / `Delete` / `Escape` contentEditable paths.

### Confidence: 3/5
Moderate confidence from a full-branch code review plus category sweeps across rendering, accessibility, API/state design, maintainability, performance, and tests. The biggest remaining uncertainty is in the browser-specific `contentEditable` interaction paths, which are large and only lightly exercised at the component level.

## Claude code (Opus 4.6) review

### Overview

This PR adds three new temporal field components (`DateField`, `TimeField`, `DateTimeField`) with shared infrastructure including a central `TemporalFieldStore`, format parser, adapter pattern, caching layer, and localization support. The architecture follows established Base UI patterns (class-based `ReactStore`, memoized selectors, `useRenderElement`).

---

### Blockers

#### 1. Typo in error message — `TemporalAdapterContext.ts:23`
```
'Base UI: TemporalAdapterContext is missing. Temporal components must be place within <TemporalAdapterProvider />'
```
Should be `"must be placed within"`. Every other context error in the codebase uses "placed".

#### 2. Error message formatting inconsistency — `TemporalAdapterContext.ts:23`
The error message is also missing a trailing period. Every other context error in the codebase ends with `.` (e.g., `"must be placed within <Switch.Root>."`).

---

### Potential Bugs

#### 3. `sectionEventHandlers` attached to separators — `DateFieldSection.tsx:53`
`store.sectionEventHandlers` is spread onto **every** section element, including separators. While the event handlers do early-return when `getSectionIndexFromDOMElement` returns null for non-date-part elements, this is wasteful and adds `onKeyDown`, `onInput`, `onPaste`, `onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onClick`, `onMouseUp`, and `onDragOver` to inert separator `<div>`s. Consider conditionally attaching handlers only to date part sections.

#### 4. `onBlur` setTimeout(0) race condition with unmount
```ts
// TemporalFieldStore.ts:930
this.timeoutManager.startTimeout('blur-detection', 0, () => {
  const activeEl = this.getActiveElement();
  const isInsideField = !!this.rootRef.current?.contains(activeEl);
  ...
});
```
`mountEffect` cleanup calls `this.timeoutManager.clearAll()`, so this is safe on normal unmount. In StrictMode (double mount/unmount), if blur fires between the first unmount and second mount, the timeout might produce stale behavior. Worth verifying in StrictMode.

#### 5. `clearActive` doesn't explicitly preserve focus/selection after DOM sync
`clearActive` is called from `onInput` but doesn't re-assert the section selection after `syncDatePartContentToDOM` runs (which replaces `textContent` and calls `syncSelectionToDOM`). In practice the section likely retains focus since it triggered the input event, but the `textContent` replacement could cause the browser to collapse the selection. If this isn't already covered by the `syncSelectionToDOM` observer set up in `mountEffect`, it could lose the section highlight.

---

### Edge Cases

#### 6. No keyboard shortcut for full-field paste
When a user pastes a complete date string into a section, the `onPaste` handler falls through to `updateFromString` if the pasted value doesn't match the section's content type. This is good. But there's no handling for Ctrl+A → paste at the root level to replace the entire field value in one action. Is this intentional?

#### 7. Weekday parsing: `shouldSkipWeekDays` only activates when `day` is also present
```ts
// TemporalFieldStore.ts:1178-1181
const shouldSkipWeekDays = sectionsList.some(
  (section) => isDatePart(section) && section.token.config.part === 'day',
);
```
If a format has only a weekday **without** a day-of-month section (exotic edge case), the weekday would be included in the date-parsing string. The comment documents the `dayjs` limitation, but this could silently produce wrong results with certain format strings.

#### 8. Adapter cache is per-instance — inline `new TemporalAdapterDateFns()` defeats it
The `WeakMap` in `adapter-cache.ts` is keyed by adapter instance. If a consumer writes `<TemporalAdapterProvider adapter={new TemporalAdapterDateFns()}>` inline in JSX, a new adapter instance is created every render and the cache is rebuilt each time. This could cause perf issues. Worth documenting as a usage guideline.

---

### Code Quality & Readability

#### 9. Store file size — `TemporalFieldStore.ts` (~1550 lines)
The method grouping is logical (publish, edit, adjust, DOM sync), but the file is large. The editing logic (`applyNumericEditing`, `applyLetterEditing`, `applyQuery`) and character-query state machine could potentially be extracted into a separate module to improve navigability.

#### 10. `mountEffect` is an arrow property, not a method
```ts
// TemporalFieldStore.ts:293
public mountEffect = () => { ... };
```
This creates a new function per instance (to preserve `this` binding for `useOnMount`). Other methods in the class are regular methods. Minor inconsistency — consider documenting why this is an arrow property, or making `registerSection` (which is also an arrow property for the same reason) and `mountEffect` consistent with the rest.

#### 11. `React.createRef` in non-component class
```ts
public readonly rootRef = React.createRef<HTMLDivElement>();
hiddenInputRef: React.createRef<HTMLInputElement>(),
```
`React.createRef` works fine here (it just returns `{ current: null }`), but using a plain `{ current: null }` would be more idiomatic since `TemporalFieldStore` is not a React component. Not a blocker.

#### 12. Redundant `index` parameter in `SectionList.children`
`DateFieldSectionList` renders `sections.map(children)`, so `children` receives `(section, index)` from `Array.prototype.map`. But sections already carry `section.index`. If these are always identical, the second parameter is redundant API surface. If they can differ, this is a potential source of confusion — document the difference.

---

### Pattern Compliance ✅

| Guideline | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| Store pattern (`ReactStore` class) | ✅ Matches Dialog, Calendar, Tooltip, Menu, etc. |
| Selector pattern (`createSelector`/`createSelectorMemoized`) | ✅ |
| `useRenderElement` | ✅ Used in Section, Clear; Root delegates to hook |
| `TimeoutManager` instead of raw `setTimeout` | ✅ |
| No `requestAnimationFrame` or raw `setTimeout` | ✅ Confirmed |
| No misused `useCallback`/`useLayoutEffect` | ✅ |
| Re-export pattern (TimeField/DateTimeField → DateField parts) | ✅ |
| Field integration (`useField`, `useLabelableId`, etc.) | ✅ |
| Event details (`createChangeEventDetails`) | ✅ |

---

### Test Coverage

Test structure is solid:
- **Unit tests**: Character editing, value adjustment, format parsing, edge dates, section management, field integration, element props, adapter cache
- **Integration tests**: Shared across all 3 field types
- **Interaction tests**: DOM behavior
- **Translation tests**: aria-labels
- **SectionList tests**: Rendering

Noted gaps:
- No explicit StrictMode test for the blur timeout race condition
- No test for exotic RTL formats
- No test verifying adapter cache invalidation when adapter instance changes

---

### Summary

| Category | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Blockers | 2 (typo + error message formatting) |
| Potential bugs | 3 |
| Edge case gaps | 3 |
| Code quality notes | 4 |

The implementation is well-structured and follows established Base UI patterns closely. The blockers are quick copy-edit fixes. The potential bugs around separator event handlers and blur race conditions are worth investigating but are unlikely to cause user-facing issues. Overall this is solid work.

GPT Pro review

1. **`timezone` prop changes do not rebuild the rendered sections.**
   `useTemporalFieldRoot` syncs `timezoneProp` into store state, and the timezone helper gives `timezoneProp` precedence, but the only effect that reparses the format and rebuilds `sections` listens only to `rawFormat`, `adapter`, `direction`, `translations`, `min`, and `max`. On top of that, `buildSections()` formats each token with `adapter.formatByString(date, element.value)` and receives no timezone input. That means changing `timezone` without also changing `value`/`format` can leave the visible month/day/hour text stale. I’d treat this as a blocker.

2. **The hidden-input `'invalid'` sentinel will not trigger native `badInput` for `date`/`time`/`datetime-local`.**
   The selector explicitly writes `'invalid'` for partially filled fields “to trigger badInput”, but the backing inputs are native `type="date"`, `type="time"`, and `type="datetime-local"`. For those input types, invalid values are sanitized to the empty string, and `badInput` is about the browser’s UI failing to convert user input, not about assigning an arbitrary invalid string in code. So a partially filled field will collapse to “empty” at the native input layer instead of surfacing the intended invalid state. I’d also treat this as a blocker for form integration.

3. **Localized-digit weekday editing can yield `undefined`.**
   Numeric edits are routed through `applyNumericEditing`, and `cleanDigitDatePartValue()` localizes the returned digits; the examples even call out Arabic numerals. But in the weekday special-case, the code indexes the weekday array with `Number(response.datePartValue) - 1`. If `response.datePartValue` is a localized digit such as `٢`, `Number(...)` parses to `NaN`, so the weekday lookup becomes `weekdays[NaN]`, and that `undefined` value is then forwarded as the new section value. This looks like a real locale regression.

The fixes I’d try first are: rebuild sections on timezone changes and format them in the render timezone; stop relying on an invalid string in native date/time inputs for partial-state validation; and normalize localized digits back with `removeLocalizedDigits()` before calling `Number(...)` in the weekday path.

Posting an Opus 4.6 review while I'm doing a manual review myself.

**Branch:** `flaviendelangle/date-field-component` (commit 254d0af)
**Scope:** 185 files, +20,114 / -259 lines — `DateField`, `TimeField`, `DateTimeField`

---

### 1. Remaining Bugs / Issues

#### 1a. `computeAriaValueText` doesn't normalize localized digits (medium severity)

In adapter-cache.ts, the digit weekDay branch does:

```ts
const dateWithWeekDay = adapter.addDays(startOfWeekDate, Number(section.value) - 1);
```

When the adapter locale produces localized digits (e.g., Arabic `٢`), `Number(section.value)` yields `NaN` because `removeLocalizedDigits()` is never called here. The editing path in `TemporalFieldStore.applyNumericEditing` correctly calls `removeLocalizedDigits()` before `Number(...)`, but the aria computation does not. The same issue applies to the digit month branch (`Number(section.value) - 1` at line ~399) and the digit day branch (`Number(section.value)` at line ~410).

**Fix:** Add `removeLocalizedDigits(section.value, getLocalizedDigits(adapter))` in `computeAriaValueText` before every `Number(section.value)` conversion.

#### 1b. Hidden input for partially-filled fields returns `''` rather than triggering `badInput` (known — addressed since GPT Pro review)

The `stringifyValueForHiddenInput` functions return `''` for invalid values. With native `<input type="date">`, assigning `''` sets the input to empty — not to a bad-input state. This means a partially-filled (invalid) field will look "empty" to constraint validation rather than "invalid." Per the GPT Pro review, the latest commit (2d1d2fe) is supposed to address this, but reviewing dateFieldConfig.ts, timeFieldConfig.ts, and dateTimeFieldConfig.ts still shows only `return ''` for `!adapter.isValid(value)`. 

**Status:** Appears still unresolved. The hidden input will report `valueMissing` (if required) instead of `typeMismatch`/`badInput` for partially-filled fields. This affects form validation accuracy.

#### 1c. `cleanActiveDateSectionsIfValueNull` timeout can stale-close over value

In TemporalFieldStore.ts, the `setTimeout(0)` callback captures `currentValue` and compares it with `this.state.value`. If two rapid edits to different sections both set `activeDate == null`, the second timeout will run after the first has already modified `sections`. The check `this.state.value === currentValue` guards against value changes but not against stale section references. In practice this is very unlikely to trigger a visible bug (the sections are immediately rebuilt), but the pattern is fragile.

## GPT-5.4 Pro Review

I like the direction overall. The shared temporal core looks strong, and the accessibility work is thoughtful. But I would still treat this as **not merge-ready yet** because the PR is very large — about **+20,597 / -274 across 186 files** — so any public-API ambiguity here will be expensive to unwind later. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/3666/files)][1])

What I would change before merge:

1. **Tighten the public types first.**
   The author explicitly notes that the `TValue` generic is still effectively a broad temporal-field object type for now, and the generated API tables reflect that: `DateField`/`TimeField` expose `value` and `defaultValue` as `TemporalValue`, while `referenceDate`, `min`, and `max` show up as `Date`. For three distinct public components, that feels too loose and internally inconsistent. I would not love merging a public API that the author already describes as something to rethink later. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/3666)][2])

2. **Narrow the `format` contract in docs, or strengthen runtime validation.**
   The docs currently say the `format` string follows **date-fns format patterns**, but the parser is adapter-driven, and the runtime only supports a subset of parts: `weekDay`, `day`, `month`, `year`, `hours`, `minutes`, `seconds`, and `meridiem`. Unsupported parts only trigger a development warning. That means the docs currently promise more than the implementation guarantees, and “date-fns patterns” is especially misleading if another adapter is active. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/docs/src/app/%28docs%29/react/components/date-field/page.mdx)][3])

3. **Pick one primary composition model, or document the split much more clearly.**
   `Root` accepts a render function for sections, but `useTemporalFieldRoot` silently wraps that in `SectionList`; `SectionList` itself just maps sections and **does not render a wrapper element**. At the same time, the hand-written docs say `SectionList` “groups all sections into a single element,” which is simply not true. The result is a public API with two ways to render sections, plus JSDoc that suggests wrapper flexibility the implementation does not really provide in the “children as function” path. I would either make `SectionList` the clearly canonical layout primitive, or keep the `Root` callback as undocumented sugar. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/packages/react/src/date-field/utils/useTemporalFieldRoot.tsx)][4])

4. **Fix the repeated-part accessibility bug.**
   The hidden per-part labels are generated by mapping all date parts and giving each span an id based on `section.token.config.part`, and each segment’s `aria-labelledby` points to `${id}-${part}-label`. I do not see duplicate-part rejection in format validation. So if repeated-part formats are allowed — for example a text month plus a numeric month — this will create duplicate React keys and duplicate DOM ids. That is a real bug, not just a docs concern. I’d dedupe hidden labels by part, or key/id them by section index. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/packages/react/src/date-field/utils/useTemporalFieldRoot.tsx)][4])

5. **The separator story is workable, but not first-class enough yet.**
   The good news is that `DateField.Section` does expose `separator` state and a `render` prop, so custom separator markup is possible while keeping the built-in wiring. The downside is that if a consumer replaces separators with their own nodes *outside* `DateField.Section`, they lose the built-in click-to-select behavior because that wiring lives in the section/separator handlers. React Aria’s `DateInput` → `DateSegment` model, with segment `type="literal"`, is much more obvious. I would at least tighten the JSDoc and add a demo showing the `render={(props, state) => ...}` path for separators. Longer-term, I’d seriously consider whether `separator` should actually be named `literal`. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/docs/src/app/%28docs%29/react/components/date-field/types.md)][5])

6. **The imperative focus story feels underpowered.**
   `Root` renders a `div` plus a hidden input, `inputRef` points at the hidden input, and `actionsRef` only exposes `clear`. That means programmatic focus is available only through an implementation-detail ref rather than a field-shaped public action. A `focus()` action would make this API feel more complete and easier to use from forms and validation flows. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/docs/src/app/%28docs%29/react/components/date-field/types.md)][5])

7. **There is a meaningful React Aria parity gap in the semantic API.**
   Base UI currently offers a lower-level surface: `format`, `timezone`, `referenceDate`, and for time/date-time, `ampm` and `step`. React Aria pairs its segmented model with semantic props like `granularity`, `hourCycle`, `hideTimeZone`, `placeholderValue`, and `isDateUnavailable`, plus an explicit `DateInput` container with its own state surface. Base UI’s token-level `format` is actually *more powerful* for exact layouts like `EEEE, MMMM dd, yyyy` or `yyyy-MM-dd`, but it also makes the component easier to misuse and much harder to document precisely. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/docs/src/app/%28docs%29/react/components/date-field/types.md)][5])

8. **I’m uneasy about zoned form submission semantics.**
   The field logic preserves the input timezone when publishing `onValueChange`, but the form-facing hidden inputs for `TimeField` and `DateTimeField` serialize to native `time` and `datetime-local` strings. My inference is that this drops timezone information on submit, whereas React Aria documents form submission as ISO 8601 strings. If zoned values are a real target use case, I’d either document this limitation very plainly or add an alternate hidden ISO value path. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/packages/react/src/date-field/utils/TemporalFieldStore.ts)][6])

What looks especially good:

* **The shared architecture is the right call.** `TimeField` and `DateTimeField` reuse the same `Section`, `SectionList`, and `Clear` parts, which is exactly in the spirit of AGENTS.md’s guidance to avoid duplicating logic and to centralize shared behavior. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/master/AGENTS.md)][7])

* **The accessibility model is thoughtful.** Individual sections are exposed as spinbuttons, they get field-level and part-level labeling, and the code clearly propagates error/description context down to each editable segment. That’s a solid baseline. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/flaviendelangle/base-ui/raw/refs/heads/date-field-component/packages/react/src/date-field/utils/selectors.ts)][8])

* **The PR does put serious effort into docs and tests.** It adds dedicated docs pages/demos and a sizable set of component and shared tests for the new field family. So this is not a “half-documented” feature; the remaining issues are mostly about *accuracy and clarity* of the public contract, not lack of effort. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/3666/files)][1])

On AGENTS.md specifically: I’d say this is **mostly conformant on the code side** and **not fully there on the docs side**. The implementation shares logic well, uses the DOM-safe owner utilities AGENTS asks for, and clearly invested in tests/docs. The main miss is that some hand-written docs still overstate or contradict the actual API behavior, and AGENTS explicitly says public docs should be updated accurately when the API changes. ([[GitHub](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/master/AGENTS.md)][7])

My net: **promising implementation, but I would block on 1–4**. The React Aria gap is not that Base UI lacks power; it’s that React Aria’s model is currently easier to understand and harder to misuse.
